To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified a BoNT-like protein in a commensal Enterococcus species, determined its molecular structure, identified its host target proteins, and determined its genetic context.
we have identified a novel botulinum neurotoxin-like toxin in a commensal strain of Enterococcus faecium.

we have identified a novel botulinum neurotoxin-like protein in a commensal Enterococcus faceium strain and determined that it cleaves VAMP2 and SNARE-25, the proteins that mediate neurotransmitter release in neurons, at distinct sites from known BoNT cleavage sites on these proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a BoNT-like gene from the commensal bacterium, Enterococcus fa...
the identification of a novel BoNT-like toxin in a commensal strain of Enterococcus faecium.
the identification of a novel BoNT-like toxin from E. faeceum, and its possible role as a pathogenic factor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a commensal strain of enterococci carries a BoNT gene cluster and produces a BoNT-like protein that cleaves both Vamp2 and SNAP- 25 at distinct cleavage sites.
the E. faecium strain carrying the toxin is a commensally acquired organism and that the toxin gene is located on a putatively conjugative 206 kb plasmid.
the BoNT gene cluster in E. faeium is not the same as the one in C. botulinum and is likely to be a result of a lateral gene transfer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified a BoNT-like neurotoxin in a commensal strain of E.  faecium and determined that the BoNT-like gene is located within an extended BoNT gene cluster that is present on a putatively conjugative 206 kb plasmid.
the E. faecium strain carrying a BoNT/En-like gene cluster was isolated from cow fecal sample, which was identified as a commensal strain by whole genome sequencing and phylogenetic analysis.
we discovered a new botulinum neurotoxin-like toxin in a commensal strain of Enterococcus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
commensal E. faeium strains can acquire BoNT gene clusters and produce a BoNT-like neurotoxin, which may have potential bioterrorist applications.
the commensal E. faeciun strain carrying a BoNT gene cluster can serve as a potential source of BoNTs.
a commensal strain of E.  faecium carries a BoNT/En toxin that cleaves both Vamp2 and SNAP25 at sites different from known BoNT cleavage sites.
